title: George Romero Wrote a Resident Evil Movie You Never Saw
hook: In 1998 George Romero, the director of Night of the Living Dead, shot a Resident Evil 2 commercial for Capcom and then wrote a faithful Resident Evil movie script. Capcom dropped it at E3 1999. Would you have rather seen his version?
script: Did you know the father of the zombie movie once directed a Resident Evil commercial? In 1998, Capcom hired George Romero, the man behind Night of the Living Dead, to shoot a live action TV spot for Biohazard 2. That is what Resident Evil 2 is called in Japan. The thirty second ad starred Brad Renfro as Leon and Adrienne Frantz as Claire, and it aired only in Japan. Then Constantin Film and Sony hired Romero to write and direct a full Resident Evil movie. His first draft was dated October 7th, 1998. It stuck close to the first game, with Chris Redfield, Jill Valentine, Albert Wesker, the mansion, zombie dogs, and the Tyrant. He wrote several more drafts after that. Then at E3 in 1999, Capcom producer Yoshiki Okamoto told Electronic Gaming Monthly that the script was not good, so Romero was fired. Paul W. S. Anderson took over. His 2002 film invented a brand new hero named Alice, played by Milla Jovovich, who never appeared in the games. Anderson wrote all six films, and the series grossed about 1.2 billion dollars worldwide. Romero's faithful version was never made. Would you have rather seen Romero's Resident Evil? Follow for more gaming history.
